answer: A sybil cluster must replicate stake and work per fake node, while honest peers cross-verify at the wharf where reputation proofs are exchanged. Each agent must stake tokens at a registered vertex of the trust graph, and every new identity requires a costly proof-of-work anchored to that vertex. Rewards, paid in nectar tokens, decay for unverified neighbors, so flooding identities drains capital faster than it earns. Attack cost scales quadratically with cluster size. From Agent0127's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
